title: Gluten-Free Ginger Molasses Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft gluten-free spice cupcakes with molasses and ginger, ready in about 43 minutes with a tangy cream cheese swirl on top.
description: These cupcakes taste like a warm spice cookie in cake form. Molasses and fresh ginger give the crumb a deep, cozy flavor without being heavy. I tested this batter three times to get a gluten-free flour blend that stays soft instead of gritty. The cream cheese swirl on top balances the sweetness with a little tang. They work for fall parties, but honestly I make them in July too. Ginger and molasses do not need a season to taste good. This is a one-bowl batter, so cleanup is easy. No mixer required if your arm is willing to whisk for a minute.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups gluten-free all-purpose flour blend (with xanthan gum)
1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted and slightly cooled
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
In a medium bowl, whisk the gluten-free flour, baking soda, salt, ginger, cinnamon, and cloves.
In a large bowl, whisk melted butter, molasses, and brown sugar until smooth.
Whisk in the egg, then the buttermilk and fresh ginger until combined.
Add the dry mix to the wet mix. Stir just until no dry streaks remain.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
Beat cream cheese and softened butter until smooth, about 1 minute.
Add powdered sugar and vanilla. Beat until fluffy and no lumps remain.
Once cupcakes are fully cool, swirl or pipe the cream cheese frosting on top.
tips: Room temperature egg and buttermilk mix in faster and give an even crumb.
Do not overbake. Molasses cupcakes dry out fast if you push past 18 minutes.
If your gluten-free blend has no xanthan gum, add 1/4 tsp to the dry mix.
Chill the frosted cupcakes 10 minutes before serving so the swirl holds its shape in warm rooms.

faq.question: Can I use dark molasses instead of regular?
faq.answer: Yes, but use blackstrap sparingly since it is more bitter. Regular unsulphured molasses gives the best balance for this batter.

faq.question: Why did my gluten-free cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means the pan was underbaked or the blend lacked xanthan gum. Test with a toothpick at 16 minutes and add gum if your blend does not include it.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy-free too?
faq.answer: Swap the butter for a plant-based stick and use dairy-free cream cheese and a dairy-free milk with 1 tsp lemon juice in place of buttermilk.

faq.question: How long do these cupcakes stay fresh?
faq.answer: Store frosted cupcakes covered in the fridge for up to 4 days. Let them sit at room temperature 15 minutes before eating for the best texture.

conclusion: These cupcakes prove spice cake does not need to wait for fall. Warm ginger, deep molasses, and a tangy swirl make them worth baking any month.
